title: A Vesicle Needs Three Separate Steps

scenes.tts: A yeast mutant called sec one grows at twenty-five degrees Celsius. At thirty-seven degrees it keeps making secretory enzymes, but they stay inside. The pool inside rises up to eightfold, packed into membrane-bound vesicles. These vesicles formed, so budding worked. Something later failed.
scenes.caption: A yeast mutant called sec1 grows at 25 °C. At 37 °C it keeps making secretory enzymes, but they stay inside. The pool inside rises up to eightfold, packed into membrane-bound vesicles. These vesicles formed, so budding worked. Something later failed.
scenes.visual: A yeast cell fills with vesicles that pile up inside; an enzyme-pool bar climbs to up to 8 times; a red question mark sits between the pile and the surface.
scenes.narration: A yeast mutant called sec1 grows at 25 °C. At 37 °C it keeps making secretory enzymes, but they stay inside. The pool inside rises up to eightfold, packed into membrane-bound vesicles. These vesicles formed, so budding worked. Something later failed.

scenes.tts: A vesicle first needs a coat. At the E R, a small switch called Sar one binds the membrane when it carries GTP. Sar one brings in the Sec twenty-three twenty-four complex. That complex brings in the outer cage. Together they make COP two. The coat grabs the cargo and bends the membrane into a bud.
scenes.caption: A vesicle first needs a coat. At the ER, a small switch called Sar1 binds the membrane when it carries GTP. Sar1 brings in the Sec23/24 complex. That complex brings in the outer cage. Together they make COPII. The coat grabs the cargo and bends the membrane into a bud.
scenes.visual: Sar1-GTP lands on the ER membrane, Sec23/24 and the outer cage stack on it, then become a coat that gathers cargo and bows the membrane into a bud that pinches off.
scenes.narration: A vesicle first needs a coat. At the ER, a small switch called Sar1 binds the membrane when it carries GTP. Sar1 brings in the Sec23/24 complex. That complex brings in the outer cage. Together they make COPII. The coat grabs the cargo and bends the membrane into a bud.

scenes.tts: Once it has budded, the vesicle needs an address. A Rab is a small switch anchored in a membrane. With GDP bound, it is held in the cytosol by a protein called GDI. A G E F on the right membrane loads GTP, and the Rab lights up like a sign over one loading bay. It recruits tethers, long proteins that capture the vesicle.

scenes.visual: The coated vesicle waits. A GDI cup holds Rab-GDP in the cytosol; a GEF on the target membrane loads GTP so the Rab lights up; tether rods grow from it and catch the vesicle.

scenes.tts: Capture is not fusion, because two membranes resist merging. SNAREs supply the force. Four motifs, called Q a, Q b, Q c and R, wind into one bundle. The bundle zippers toward the membrane anchors and pulls the bilayers together until they fuse. Afterwards all four sit in one membrane, and N S F uses ATP to pull them apart for reuse.

scenes.visual: Three Q rods stand on the target membrane and the R rod hangs from the vesicle; the overlap zippers and the vesicle sinks and merges; the four rods lie in one membrane and NSF with ATP separates them.

scenes.tts: Test tubes show that these steps come apart. Vesicles made with G M P P N P still formed. This GTP analogue cannot be hydrolyzed, and the vesicles kept their coat and failed to target and fuse. Once vesicles had docked, fusion no longer cared about GDI, a protein that pulls Rabs off membranes. Truncated H O P S tethers still tethered liposomes, but failed to promote fusion.
scenes.caption: Test tubes show that these steps come apart. Vesicles made with GMP-PNP still formed. This GTP analogue cannot be hydrolyzed, and the vesicles kept their coat and failed to target and fuse. Once vesicles had docked, fusion no longer cared about GDI, a protein that pulls Rabs off membranes. Truncated HOPS tethers still tethered liposomes, but failed to promote fusion.
scenes.visual: A three-column table (bud, target, fuse). In each of three rows a token moves along and stops at the failing step: GMP-PNP stops after budding, GDI after docking bounces off, truncated HOPS stops before fusion.

scenes.tts: Back to sec one. A vesicle needs a coat to bud, a Rab and a tether to be caught, and SNAREs to fuse. Those vesicles formed, so the coat worked, and a later step failed. Each step can fail alone. Budding, targeting and fusion are separate steps.
